title: Landlord abroad, keys by courier
text: Hello, thanks for your interest in my apartment. My husband and I moved back abroad for family reasons so I can't show it in person, but it's exactly like the pictures. Send the deposit and first month's rent and I'll have a courier deliver the keys to your home, shipping paid by me.
advice: Never pay for a place you haven't viewed in person. A landlord who can't show it but will post the keys is the classic scam.

title: Mass viewing, first to pay wins
text: I'm the one letting the room, come see it this evening. Loads of people are viewing today, so whoever pays the deposit first gets it. Transfer it tonight and I'll give you the keys and move-in date.
advice: Don't pay a deposit at a crowded viewing. Check with the RTB or the Land Registry that the person letting it actually has the right to.

title: Deposit just to book a viewing
text: Due to a high number of no-shows we ask for a small refundable deposit to book a viewing slot. Please enter your card details on the booking page to secure your time. You may get a call from your bank's security team to confirm it.
advice: Real landlords don't charge to view. Never enter card details to book a viewing, and hang up on any 'bank' call that follows.

title: Payment link on a copycat site
text: Thanks for your email. To book your viewing please choose a date and time on this link and confirm your bank card with a 2 euro deposit, which is forfeited if you don't show. Revolut cards aren't accepted. Don't refresh or close the page while it processes.
advice: Only pay through the real site you found the listing on. Check the web address carefully before entering card details.

title: WhatsApp only, family emergency
text: I'm hard of hearing so I can only talk on WhatsApp, sorry. I'm away helping my daughter who just had a baby, so I can't meet you, but here's a video of the apartment. If you send the deposit and first month's rent I'll have the contract signed by my solicitor.
advice: Insist on a phone or video call and a viewing in person. A sad story plus 'WhatsApp only' is a common cover.

title: ID documents before any viewing
text: Before we go any further please send me a copy of your passport or driving licence and tell me a bit about yourself. Once you transfer the deposit and a month's rent I'll arrange to send you the keys.
advice: Don't send your passport or licence before you've viewed and agreed a lease. Scammers reuse them for fraud.

title: Real listing, different contact details
text: Yes the house on the listing is still available, but please contact me directly on this number rather than through the site. I can't do viewings at the moment, but I can send more photos, and once rent and deposit are paid I'll post the keys.
advice: Contact the landlord only through the listing site. A request to move to a new number or email is a red flag.

title: Untraceable payment requested
text: I can't take card payments, please send the deposit by Revolut or crypto, or wire it to my account in another country. Cash is also fine if you prefer. Once it lands I'll confirm the room is yours.
advice: Never pay rent or a deposit by crypto, gift cards, Western Union, cash or to a foreign account. Use a traceable bank transfer after you've viewed and signed.

title: Discount to deal off the platform
text: If you book with me directly instead of through the website I can give you a better price, as the site charges me fees. Just email me and I'll send my bank details for the deposit.
advice: Stay on the platform. A discount for paying directly removes every protection you had.

title: Pay today, lease later
text: This is a one-time offer and I have lots of people asking, so I need the deposit and first month's rent today or it goes to the next person. No need for references, we can sort the lease out after you've paid.
advice: Don't be rushed. Get a written lease and view the property before any money changes hands.
